verifier: bd1 (max2 round 2, adversarial card verifier: burdam, dunsom)
method: Read every shipped card in art/out/fighters/{burdam,dunsom} at full size, at card size (480 px wide), at 128 and 64 px (LANCZOS, then enlarged nearest-neighbour for viewing), plus 3-4x face crops; painted portraits A/B against their 3D references in art/.cache/fighters/paint/<sid>_<kind>_3d.png (mean abs RGB diff and by eye). Re-ran card_qa.py burdam dunsom (exit 1: blank tripwire on all 6 splashes, Burdam base portrait and Stillwater portrait) and node tools/gen_store.ts --check (store.json current, dE gate 32/32 pass).
cardQa: fails: blank tripwire on burdam splash 0.76, burdam portrait 0.65 (at threshold), burdam_stillwater splash 0.91 and portrait 0.91, burdam_almanac splash 0.84, dunsom splash 0.87, dunsom_highrim splash 0.77, dunsom_almanac splash 0.82; passes: burdam_almanac portrait 0.64, dunsom portrait 0.44, dunsom_highrim portrait 0.39, dunsom_almanac portrait 0.34
scoreNote: Gauge only: a recent LoL splash is a painted, dynamic, face-forward figure with strong value design. Both fighters' round-1 sensitivity blockers are fixed at the model (Burdam: lidded eyes with pupils instead of hollow holes; Dunsom: no cracks, lidded eyes with pupils). But all six splashes are still the clean 3D finish on a painted plate (a clay-figure look over a painterly ground, single-hue lighting, small static figures), and the painted portraits are hardly painted (mean diff vs 3D 2.5-8.5 of 255: a regrade, not added painted form). Dunsom's face is a small mouthless flat slab under a wide hat, so its cards depend on 2-3 px eyes.

perCard.issues: At 4x the mask now has carved brows, lidded eyes with brown pupils, nose and frown (the round-1 hollow holes are gone). But the head is about 2 % of the frame height: at card size (480) and at 128 it reads as a bare pale egg with no features (card_qa blank 0.76 agrees), and the peach figure sinks into the orange domes behind it. Fails card_qa's blank gate, and by eye it is a blank-face read at card size.

Cleared by eye despite card_qa blank 0.65 (exactly at the 0.65 threshold): at 512, 128 and 64 the carved mask shows two lidded eyes with dark pupils, heavy brows, a nose and a frown; no hollow, glow, crack, streak or skull read. Same pose, silhouette, palette and parts as the 3D render (the paint only cools the scarf a little; diff 8.5). Minor: barely painted; the forehead tally marks read as hash glyphs, not text. Ships only with this by-eye clearance recorded.

At 3x the bowed face has lidded eyes with pupils, but at card size the bowed bald dome dominates and the face reads as a featureless pale egg sunk into the purple scarf (card_qa blank 0.84). Blank-face read at card size; 3D figure on a painted plate.

Passes card_qa (blank 0.64, a hair under the threshold) and by eye: both lidded eyes with pupils show under the brows at 512 and 128; at 64 the eyes are faint dark slits but the face still reads as a stern carved face, not a skull. On-model with the render (diff 3.5): same bowed pose, scarf, tallies, no invented part. Borderline at 64; quality is a regrade, not a painting.

The raised forearm and pauldron hide the lower half of the face (only one eye shows), and the bowed bald dome reads as a blank pale egg at card size (card_qa blank 0.91). Pose hides the face; blank-face read.

The two chin tally groups under the frown read as a stitched mouth at 512 and 128 (a horror lean), and card_qa blank 0.91 fails. Also a record mismatch: paint.json lists 'shipped: painted, variant 1', but the shipped file is pixel-identical to art/.cache/fighters/paint/burdam_stillwater_portrait_3d.png (mean diff 0.0). The lane already holds this card for the TALLY_CHIN = [] rebuild. The 3D icon also shows the chin tallies (a note; icons are outside this verdict).

At 2x the face is a flat mouthless ochre slab with small lidded eyes and a nose, framed by a cream hood wrap and a wound linen scarf over the lower face and chest. At card size the face is a blank peach block inside wrapped bands: a blank-face and mummy-wrap read (card_qa blank 0.87). The figure is one peach value against an orange plate.

On-model with the render (diff 2.5) and clean at 4x (lidded eyes with pupils, no crack or streak), but the 'portrait' frames the whole upper body under the lantern, so the face is about 25 % of the frame width. At 128 and 64 it reads as a pale, featureless block wrapped in cream linen: the blank-face and mummy-wrap read the blocker list names. card_qa (blank 0.44) misses it because it samples the face disc at 128 px from the full-res card. Fix: crop tighter on the face (the face at about 40 % of the frame width) and give the mask more value contrast against the wrap.

At 3x the dark-rose mask has lidded eyes with pupils and the raised hand is a fist (the round-1 claw spikes are gone), but at card size the face is a blank block under the hat inside a white wrap (card_qa blank 0.82). The fist is a rough low-detail block at 3x.

Default to fail: at 4x the dark lacquer mask has pale amber lidded eyes with pupils (not glowing; eye dV -7.8), but at 128 and 64 the face is a dark blank oval under the hat, and the only features are two 2-3 px pale marks that read as light-points rather than eyes. A dark mouthless face with bright eye marks at chip size leans to the blank or glowing-eye class. On-model with the render (diff 3.7, no invented prop).

The golden mask is a blank slab at card and chip size (card_qa blank 0.77); the face is about 3 % of the frame. The staff foot and feet sit at the cliff lip; they are grounded but read close to the edge.

Passes card_qa (blank 0.39) and by eye: at 512 and 128 the golden mask shows two lidded eyes with dark pupils and a nose; the raised hand is a fist on the hat brim; on-model with the render (diff 2.6). Minor: at 4x the paint brightened the nose-edge highlight into a thin pale line from the inner corner of the viewer's right eye (also in the 3D, fainter); at 1:1 and card size it does not read as a streak. Face small in the frame; at 64 the eyes are barely there.

problems.what: Every splash is the 3D finish (no painted variant passed), and every one trips card_qa's blank gate. By eye the heads are 2-3 % of the frame, so the faces fixed at the model do not read at card size: bald pale egg (Burdam) or blank slab in a wrap (Dunsom). The live CDN cards stay.
problems.fix: Reframe the splash camera so the head is larger (or turn the face to camera and light it with a value break against the plate), then paint again under ruling 30. A cleared blank tripwire should come from a readable face, not from a lower threshold.

problems.what: The portrait camera frames the upper body and lantern, so the mouthless mask is a small block: blank / mummy-wrap at 128 (base) and a dark blank oval with light-point eyes at 128 and 64 (Almanac).
problems.fix: Tighten the portrait crop to head and shoulders (face at about 40 % of the frame width, lantern partly out of frame), raise the eye and lid contrast at the model, and re-run paint plus the look check.

problems.what: The chin tally groups read as a stitched mouth (horror lean); the paint.json record says painted v1 while the shipped file is the 3D reference.
problems.fix: burdam.py TALLY_CHIN = [] rebuild once ruling 32 allows it, re-render, repaint, and correct the paint.json record.

problems.what: Cleared by eye at card_qa blank 0.65 (exactly at the threshold); the painted pass is barely a painting (diff 8.5).
problems.fix: None needed for sensitivity. For quality, a stronger paint pass that keeps the face.

notes: 3 of 12 pass. Both fighters stay under par (7.5); the round-1 model blockers (hollow eyes, cracked skull, claw hands) are closed at the model. One caveat on the three passes: under the base / skin / portrait consistency rule, the passing portraits ship next to splashes that keep the pre-round-1 live versions, and those still carry the old hollow-mask (Burdam) and cracked-mask (Dunsom) faces. The lead should decide whether to ship the portraits alone or hold them until the splashes pass, so a fighter's cards do not show two different faces. Icons are 3D and were not judged; Burdam's icon shows the chin tallies.
